content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm looking for guidance on how to activate text message displays on the web server and utilize the 4 function keys on the TD for each display page. My goal is to create 6 separate text message pages, enabling remote on/off functions using the F keys. When I log in to the web server and access the TD display, I can scroll through the 6 text message pages with the up/down keys, but these pages need to be enabled or active to view them. I want to assign the 4 function keys independently for each text message page, so that each F key triggers a unique function on a specific page, rather than acting globally. For example, text message page 1 combined with the AND block and F1 key activates a particular function, while page 2 with F1 does something different. My question is, how can I enable a specific text message page in TD mode on the web server? Ideally, I would like to have 24 distinct functions—6 pages with 4 function keys each. Does anyone have suggestions to achieve this?
You need to design a menu system that activates only one text message at a time when scrolling through the message pages.
Here’s an example using 6 message pages and the F1 key to demonstrate the concept. This should help clarify the approach.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to assign unique functions to the function keys on the TD display for each individual text message page shown on the web server. The current setup only allows key functions to be applied globally rather than contextually by page, limiting flexibility. The discussion highlights the need for custom menu logic to activate only one message at a time and properly map each function key to its respective page function.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to configure the TD's function keys so that each key has a dedicated function for every text message page, allowing for context-sensitive control and maximizing the functionality of all buttons across multiple display pages.
